clue.text: His social contract wasn't British

parts.note: the writer of The Social Contract (1762) was Genevan and wrote in French, so the 'contract' is a famous treatise and its author was not British

explanation.surface: A man's social agreement was made outside Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Social Contract is the political treatise by the Geneva-born philosopher, who was French-speaking rather than British.

clue.text: Stock fare on the rigs at tea time?

definitions.text: Stock fare on the rigs at tea time?

parts.words: Stock fare on the rigs at tea time?
parts.note: pictures the snack served to oil-rig workers at tea, while it really means pressed cattle feed

explanation.surface: Asks what standard food oil-rig crews eat at tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like 'standard', but it is livestock: the fare is cattle feed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressed seed residue after oil extraction is fed to livestock.

clue.text: Main spars not yet gone metric, it seems

definitions.text: Main spars not yet gone metric, it seems

parts.words: Main spars not yet gone metric, it seems
parts.note: spars on a ship's mainmast, named in a unit of length that has not been converted to metres

explanation.surface: Ship's spars still measured in old imperial units.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' means the sea or the mainsail, and the spars carry the name of an imperial unit, not metres.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the horizontal spars from which square sails hang.

clue.text: A dress-maker in the Apocrypha

indicators.note: a maker of the dress, reshaping its letters into something new

explanation.surface: A seamstress who appears in the Apocrypha.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maker' tells you to rework the letters of A DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Two books of the Apocrypha bear the name of the scribe and priest of the Jewish return from exile.

clue.text: Turning patch inside out's a repair that's simple

indicators.note: turning the patch over suggests these letters are flipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Flipping a patch inside out is an easy mend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' shuffles PATCH INSIDE OUTS, all fifteen letters including the S of out's.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive or plain, lacking sophistication.

clue.text: "The flannelled fools at the ——" (Kipling)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Kipling's poem The Islanders, mocking cricketers in white flannels

explanation.surface: A line from Kipling with its last word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's 1902 poem The Islanders scorns 'the flannelled fools at the wicket'; cricket is the British bat-and-ball game whose players wear white flannel trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the stumps and the pitch between them are where the batsmen in flannels stand.

clue.text: His mother's painter kept his spirits up

definitions.text: His mother's painter kept his spirits up

parts.words: His mother's painter kept his spirits up
parts.note: the American who painted a famous portrait of his mother, and anyone who stays cheerful by making a tune with pursed lips

explanation.surface: A painter of his mother who stayed cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: James McNeill painted 'Arrangement in Grey and Black', known as his mother's portrait; one who whistles keeps cheerful.

clue.text: Sleepy-sounding stone-breaker

indicators.note: the word for someone sleepy is said, giving a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: someone sleepy is a napper, given to dozing

explanation.surface: A drowsy-sounding man who breaks rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A flint-worker who chips stones into shape by striking them.

clue.text: Is it the rule in God's own country?

definitions.text: Is it the rule in God's own country?

parts.words: Is it the rule in God's own country?
parts.note: 'God's own country' is a boast for a land; read literally, a country ruled by God

explanation.surface: Asks what custom holds in a much-praised land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rule' looks like a custom; it is government, by God.
explanation.definitionFit: Government by priests in the name of a deity.

clue.text: It's related Capone didn't shame the devil !

parts.note: AL, the first name of the gangster Al Capone
the proverb is 'tell the truth and shame the devil', so not shaming him means telling a falsehood: LIED

explanation.surface: A gangster failed to tell the truth and so escaped shaming the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied means connected or akin, as in allied trades.

clue.text: No need to cry over this, my pretty maid

definitions.text: No need to cry over this, my pretty maid

parts.words: No need to cry over this, my pretty maid
parts.note: combines the proverb 'no use crying over spilt milk' with the nursery rhyme milkmaid, 'Where are you going to, my pretty maid?'

explanation.surface: Someone consoles a girl who is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: The milkmaid of the nursery rhyme carries a pail; the proverb says not to weep over milk that has gone over the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that has slopped out of its container is what the proverb says is not worth tears.

clue.text: Five lay out in the wet to keep mine safe

indicators.note: the letters for five and the jumbled word are placed inside the word meaning wetness

parts.note: the wet means damp
V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: out signals the word lay is put into a different order

explanation.surface: Five people lie outdoors in the rain, keeping a mine safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' makes YLA from LAY; V and YLA go inside DAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphry Davy's lamp kept its flame behind gauze so it would not ignite firedamp, keeping coal pits safe.

clue.text: Theme about right for this circle

indicators.note: about means the word for theme goes around the letter for right

parts.note: a theme is a topic

explanation.surface: A subject concerning what is right for a particular circle of people.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines of latitude, circles round the globe.

clue.text: Drink for a Mason?

definitions.meaning: an alcoholic drink made from fermented pears
Erle Stanley Gardner's fictional lawyer Mason has this first name

explanation.surface: Something to drink for a Freemason.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both pear cider and the forename of the fictional defence lawyer Mason.

clue.text: Patricia, difficult student, with taking ways

indicators.note: a difficult person is awkward, so the name's letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Patricia, a troublesome pupil, has charming manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ways' looks like charm; here it is taking what is not yours.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates take goods by force, so taking ways describe a sea-robber.

clue.text: It's novel where "the child is father of the man"

definitions.text: It's novel where "the child is father of the man"

parts.words: It's novel where "the child is father of the man"
parts.note: Wordsworth's line taken literally: in F. Anstey's 1882 novel a father and his son swap bodies

explanation.surface: Seems to praise a new idea while quoting Wordsworth's poem about childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'new', but it is a book: Anstey's comic novel where father and son exchange places.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'the other way round', fitting a story where son becomes father and father son.

clue.text: How not to impart knowledge to developing photographers !

definitions.text: How not to impart knowledge to developing photographers !

parts.words: How not to impart knowledge to developing photographers !
parts.note: to inform, and also literally to let light in, which ruins film being developed

explanation.surface: Warning against teaching budding photographers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' looks like learning, but means developing film, which light spoils.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct or inform someone; literally to let in light.

clue.text: Hunt said to turn out in pink

indicators.note: turn out suggests the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hunt said he would appear in pink hunting coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pink' looks like a colour, or a red hunting coat; it is the garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The genus of garden flowers including carnations and sweet williams, commonly called pinks.

clue.text: Confident bets made by Garibaldi's men ?

definitions.meaning: staking one's shirt on red at roulette: bets of everything one owns
the volunteers who followed Garibaldi in unifying Italy, named for their red tunics

explanation.surface: Gamblers make sure wagers among Garibaldi's soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Garibaldi's followers wore scarlet tunics; to 'bet one's shirt' is to stake everything.

clue.text: Often boring-still he keeps us agape

definitions.text: Often boring-still he keeps us agape

parts.words: Often boring-still he keeps us agape
parts.note: drilling teeth while patients sit open-mouthed, punned as being tedious yet amazing

explanation.surface: A dull man who still leaves us astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' is drilling and 'agape' is mouths held open.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth doctor drills cavities while patients hold their mouths open.

clue.text: See 22
Commercial travels of a boy 6 dn

definitions.text: Commercial travels of a boy 6 dn

parts.words: Commercial travels of a boy 6 dn
parts.note: the trips made by a delivery boy, famously one who whistles as he goes

explanation.surface: A whistling lad's business journeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 down is the whistler; the errand boy whistling on his bicycle was a stock figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Short journeys to deliver or collect things for someone.

clue.text: Stakes getting lighter ?

explanation.surface: Wagers become less heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both a fence of pointed posts and becoming pale.

clue.text: Pop's NY address

parts.note: read as the home in New York of popular music: the district where songwriters and music publishers worked

explanation.surface: Asks where Dad lives in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like a father; it is pop music, and the 'address' is the street of music publishers in Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: The name for the cluster of New York sheet-music publishers on West 28th Street, home of popular song.

clue.text: What dishy horses !

parts.note: the word names both large serving dishes and war horses, so a horse that is a dish

explanation.surface: An exclamation admiring some good-looking horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both big flat platters and cavalry mounts.

clue.text: Conversation of little note

parts.note: small talk of no importance, with 'little note' also hinting at a chit, a short written note

explanation.surface: Talk that is not worth recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle gossip or light talk is conversation of no consequence.

clue.text: Macbeth had no spur to prick the sides of his

definitions.text: Macbeth had no spur to prick the sides of his

parts.words: Macbeth had no spur to prick the sides of his
parts.note: a quotation from Macbeth Act 1 with its last word left off: he has only ambition to drive his purpose

explanation.surface: Macbeth lacked spurs to urge on his horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth says 'I have no spur to prick the sides of my intent, but only vaulting ambition'; the missing word means his purpose.

clue.text: Turners found in parts of Kent

definitions.meaning: machines that turn wood or metal to shape it
historic administrative divisions of the county of Kent

explanation.surface: People called Turner live in parts of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England, historically divided into large districts with this old name.
explanation.definitionFit: They are both workshop turning machines and the ancient divisions of Kent.

clue.text: Mixed drink healthy if cold and wet

definitions.meaning: a cocktail of gin and beer or porter
the folk test of a hound's health is a cold, damp snout

explanation.surface: A cocktail that does you good as long as it is chilled and liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: It names an old mix of gin and beer, and the snout of a hound, said to be healthy when cold and damp.
